clue.text: Ruin Bangor's late holiday season?

parts.note: Bangor is a town in County Down, Northern Ireland, so its county is Down
fall is the American word for autumn, the season after the summer holidays

explanation.surface: Someone laments a spoiled autumn break in Bangor.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangor here is the Northern Irish town in County Down, not the Welsh city.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall is a collapse or undoing, which is what ruin means as a noun.

clue.text: Worried but stubbornly persevering

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means pursued or troubled persistently
tenacious and determined in sticking at something

explanation.surface: Anxious yet refusing to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogged means troubled persistently as a verb and tenacious as an adjective.

clue.text: Like bread with more than just the soup?

definitions.text: Like bread with more than just the soup?

parts.words: Like bread with more than just the soup?
parts.note: a type of brown bread, read as eating a complete dinner rather than only a starter

explanation.surface: A diner asks about bread to accompany more than a bowl of soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholemeal bread is made from flour using the whole grain; split, it suggests a full meal.

clue.text: Plane about to fly from vessel

indicators.note: to fly from means a piece departs the larger word

parts.note: a freighter is a cargo ship
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An aircraft is about to take off from a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'about to', but it gives RE, removed from FREIGHTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter is a military aeroplane built for air combat.

clue.text: One misses out in sale turning up after the rest?

indicators.note: misses out means a piece is left out of the word
in a down clue turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: retail is the sale of goods to the public
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone misses a bargain by arriving late at the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' turns RETAIL into LIATER, and 'misses out' drops the I to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming after the rest of something is to come subsequently, or afterwards.

clue.text: Child's first to get present in box

indicators.note: first signals that only the opening letter of the word Child's is wanted

parts.note: to present something is to offer it

explanation.surface: A child is first in line to receive a gift in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox or chest for valuables, a kind of box.

clue.text: Places sharing a deep bond

parts.note: a group of island nations whose common link is the vast Pacific, the deep, rather than any emotional tie

explanation.surface: Locations bound together by a profound connection.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the region of Pacific islands, linked to one another by the ocean.

clue.text: Fox in American's story

definitions.meaning: to fox is to baffle or confound
in American spelling a story is a level of a building

explanation.surface: A fox appears in an American tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans spell a building's storey as 'story'.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to baffle them, and a floor is also a storey of a building.

clue.text: Like some scripts looked at in auditorium, then performed

indicators.note: in an auditorium words are heard, so the pronunciation matters here

parts.note: past tense read means looked at, and it is spoken like the colour
acted means performed

explanation.surface: Scripts read through in a theatre and then staged.
explanation.definitionFit: Redacted scripts or documents have had parts edited or blacked out.

clue.text: Once again organised support in the twilight years

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a cue or arm
aged means old, in the last years of life

explanation.surface: Help given once more to the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaged means put on or arranged again, as with a show.

clue.text: King gets cheered on — go wild

indicators.note: going wild suggests the letters of the preceding words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A monarch is applauded as the crowd is urged to go wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges the letters of GETS CHEERED ON GO.
explanation.definitionFit: George II was a Hanoverian king of Great Britain, so he is an example of a king.

clue.text: Muscle shown by voter switching sides early on

indicators.note: a left letter near the start of the word swaps over to its right counterpart, as a voter might change sides

parts.note: an elector is someone entitled to vote

explanation.surface: A voter defects from one party to another early in the campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching sides early on' turns the L (left) near the front of ELECTOR into R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: An erector is a muscle that raises or holds up a body part, such as the erector spinae.

clue.text: Coming from religious writing that could be in tract

indicators.note: could be hints that the letters of the following words might be rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: A phrase that may appear in a religious pamphlet comes from scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges the letters of IN TRACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantric describes things deriving from the tantras, Hindu and Buddhist sacred texts.

clue.text: Inclination to acquire reading say — as part of this?

definitions.text: Inclination to acquire reading say — as part of this?

indicators.note: to acquire means the first word takes in the second piece inside it

parts.note: a leaning is a tendency or inclination
reading is one of the three Rs, so R stands for it

explanation.surface: A tendency to take up reading is part of education.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading, writing and arithmetic are the three Rs, so 'reading' gives R; the whole clue also defines, since reading is part of education.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquiring knowledge through study, of which reading is one part, is education in the broad sense.

clue.text: One expects no reaction from such awful ingrates

definitions.text: One expects no reaction from such

indicators.note: awful suggests the word ingrates is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: You get no response from ungrateful people.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert gases such as neon and argon hardly react chemically, so no reaction is expected.

clue.text: A place that may be seen in sea passage

parts.words: place that may be seen in sea
parts.note: an isle is a piece of land seen surrounded by sea

explanation.surface: A spot glimpsed during a sea crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a kind of passage.

clue.text: Hurried to get a bird in the van

indicators.note: to get means the first word takes the following pieces inside it

parts.note: sped means hurried
a rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to collect a bird in a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' is the vanguard, the front, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The van (vanguard) is the leading position, as is a spearhead.

clue.text: Employee giving fine performance, old union male

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
an act is a performance
TU stands for trade union

explanation.surface: A worker puts on a fine show at an old union meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is an employee who does all kinds of work.

clue.text: Man loses companion in French city

indicators.note: loses means a piece is taken out of the name

parts.note: Charles is a man's name
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A man loses his friend while in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Arles is a city in Provence in southern France, famous for its Roman remains.

clue.text: After wickedness wise man is said to be free from pretence

indicators.note: After puts the second piece behind the first

parts.note: sin means wickedness

indicators.note: is said means the word is spoken, giving another spelling

parts.note: a seer is a sage or prophet

explanation.surface: Following his sins, a sage is said to be sincere.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means genuine and honest, without any pretence.

clue.text: Aim to reach Times? One's stuck in a book

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
The Times is a newspaper, so a paper

explanation.surface: An ambition to get into The Times newspaper, by a writer stuck on a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An endpaper is the sheet glued inside the cover of a book, joining it to the pages.

clue.text: Like some food and drink when getting over depression

indicators.note: getting over means the first word spreads around the second

parts.note: ale is a drink
a dent is a depression in a surface

explanation.surface: Food and drink that help someone get over feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: Al dente describes pasta or vegetables cooked to be firm to the bite.

clue.text: Ready to move home having got personal belongings

parts.note: in means at home
gear means one's personal belongings or kit

explanation.surface: Ready to move house with all one's things packed.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle in gear has its engine engaged and is ready to move off.

clue.text: Lock up?

parts.note: not imprisonment but a lock of hair gathered high on the head

explanation.surface: A question about putting someone in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a tuft or knot of hair worn on top of the head, a lock held up.

clue.text: Composer's evasive action

definitions.meaning: Hubert ... was an English composer, known for Jerusalem
a move to ward off a blow

explanation.surface: A composer's deft dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Parry is the English composer of Jerusalem, and a parry is a defensive deflection.

clue.text: From one pressing heavily, devastating inroads

indicators.note: devastating suggests the word inroads is wrecked and its letters scattered

explanation.surface: Damaging incursions made by an oppressor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadiron is a heavy flatiron used for pressing clothes, so it presses heavily.

clue.text: Dance music — there's line in it repeated

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
repeated means the word appears twice

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Dance music with a refrain repeated over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a Latin American dance and its lively music.

clue.text: Pretended not to see what Nelson did when shaking head?

definitions.text: what Nelson did when shaking head?
definitions.meaning: at Copenhagen Admiral Nelson put his telescope to his blind eye to ignore a signal; turning one's head could literally move that eye

explanation.surface: Someone feigns not to notice, like Nelson ignoring an order.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson, blind in one eye, famously held a telescope to it at Copenhagen in 1801 to avoid seeing a signal to withdraw.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to deliberately overlook something, from Nelson's famous act of ignoring a signal.

clue.text: Month leading to border violence

parts.note: May is a month
a hem is the edge or border of cloth

explanation.surface: A month that ends with trouble at the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder or chaos.

clue.text: It sounds like a smoother system for time management

indicators.note: sounds like signals that the word is identified by how it is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a calender is a machine with rollers that smooths cloth or paper

explanation.surface: A machine that irons out schedules.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is a system dividing time into days, months and years for planning.
